note: Byte budgets for the HTML this project ships, closing the bundle half of the performance gap in docs/CONFORMANCE-GAPS.md. Bytes are exact, so these are absolute ceilings with deliberate headroom rather than ratios against a noisy measurement. Raising one is a decision: say why here, in the same commit. Measured by scripts/check_bundle_budget.py; tests/test_bundle_budget.py runs the same comparison inside make test.

rationale.playgroundPageBytes: 12 KiB against 7.4 KiB measured. The page is a single self-contained file with no external assets bar the SRI-pinned Pyodide script, and it should stay one screenful of markup plus its boot script. A 60% rise is a redesign, not a tweak.
rationale.publishedSiteBytes: 256 KiB against 110 KiB measured, sized so the rule catalog can roughly double (a whole new rule band) without the budget firing, while a build that started emitting something unintended into web/ would.
rationale.publishedPageCount: 60 against 45. One page per rule plus two indexes; 43 rules today. Catches a generator that starts writing pages nobody asked for, which a byte total alone can miss.
rationale.reportBytesAt10kFindings: 3 MiB against 2.24 MiB measured, about 235 bytes per finding. This is the number that can grow silently: a template change adding 80 bytes to a row is invisible on a fixture and adds 800 KB here. FIX-15's contract is that a 10,000-finding report stays usable, and a report that has to be downloaded before it can be read is not.
